jobs.title: RCM Coding Education Specialist
jobs.description:
OneOncology is positioning community oncologists to drive the future of medical care through a patient-centric, physician-driven, and technology-powered model to help improve the lives of everyone living with cancer and other diseases. Our team is bringing together leaders to the market place to help drive OneOncology’s mission and vision.

Why join us? This is an exciting time to join OneOncology. Our values-driven culture reflects our startup enthusiasm supported by industry leaders in oncology, urology, technology, and finance. We are looking for talented and highly-motivated individuals who demonstrate a natural desire to improve and build new processes that support the meaningful work of independent physicians and the patients they serve.

Job Description:

Role Summary:
The RCM Coding Education Specialist will report to the Manager, Coding. This role is responsible for developing, delivering, and evaluating provider-focused coding and documentation education programs that promote accurate clinical documentation, compliant coding practices, and optimal charge capture. This position serves as a subject matter expert in professional fee coding, documentation guidelines, regulatory compliance, and industry best practices while fostering a culture of continuous learning and documentation excellence across the organization.

Responsibilities:

Develop and deliver provider coding and documentation education for physicians and advanced practice providers.
Interpret and communicate coding guideline changes, payer updates, and regulatory requirements.
Conduct coding and documentation reviews to identify education opportunities and performance improvement initiatives.
Collaborate with coding, compliance, revenue cycle, and operational leaders to address coding and documentation trends.
Provide one-on-one provider coaching and specialty-specific education.
Analyze audit results, denial patterns, coding accuracy metrics, and charge capture opportunities.
Create educational materials, reference tools, and training programs to support coding compliance and documentation excellence.
Support compliance efforts through coding audits, corrective action plans, and ongoing provider education.
Serve as a trusted resource for coding, documentation, and reimbursement-related questions.
Additional responsibilities as assigned to help drive our mission of improving the lives of everyone living with cancer.

Required or Preferred Qualifications:

High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate's degree in Health Information Management, Healthcare Administration, or related field preferred.
Minimum of 2-3 years of healthcare coding, charge capture, compliance, auditing, or provider education experience.
Working knowledge of ICD-10-CM, CPT, and HCPCS coding guidelines.
Basic understanding of provider documentation requirements, medical necessity, and regulatory compliance standards.
Certified Professional Coder (CPC), Certified Coding Specialist (CCS), or equivalent credential.
Previous experience supporting physician coding education, clinical documentation improvement (CDI), or provider engagement initiatives.
Familiarity with professional fee coding, E/M coding guidelines, and Urology/Oncology-specific coding requirements.
Experience assisting with coding audits, monitoring, and education program development.
Knowledge of payer policies, reimbursement methodologies, and compliance regulations.
Experience developing educational materials, tip sheets, presentations, or provider communications.
Experience with electronic health records (EHR) and coding/billing software.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle protected health information (PHI) in accordance with HIPAA regulations.

Essential Competencies:

Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain coding concepts to providers and clinical staff.
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
Ability to analyze documentation and identify coding or documentation improvement opportunities.
Professional fee coding expertise
Provider education and coaching
Clinical documentation improvement
Compliance and regulatory knowledge
Data analysis and reporting
Revenue cycle and charge capture optimization
Communication and presentation skills
Relationship building and stakeholder engagementAttendance is an essential job function.

• Identify and mentor potential leaders, greeters, producers, and presenters.
• Co-lead NAMI trainings.
• Train and support virtual program producers and greeters.
• Identify and communicate upcoming training opportunities to leaders and prospective volunteers.
• Support and facilitate data collection and program evaluation tasks.

• Facilitate the NAMI portion of in-school presentations with community partners.

• High School Diploma or equivalent
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
• Proficiency with Zoom and comfort leading in the virtual space

• Effective communication skills, both written and verbal
• Compassion, empathy, and understanding, with strong boundaries

• Nonprofit experience highly preferred
• Volunteer management experience
• Active Colorado Peer & Family Specialist certification (required within six months of hire)

• De-escalation training

• Expected starting wage of $23 to $25 an hour.
• Health insurance plan.
• 401(k) plan (employer match determined annually based on financial results).
• Paid time off and paid holidays.
• Opportunity for some remote work.
• A flexible, supportive work environment that prioritizes self-care and work-life balance.
• Professional growth opportunities.

Send a resume and cover letter to openings@namicos.org.

This is a non-clinical peer position, ideal for someone who (1) identifies as living with a mental health condition, (2) has been in a strong place in their recovery for 2+ years, and (3) is comfortable talking about their journey.

This position reports to the Director of Programs and directly supports our peer support and education volunteers. It requires evening work, with some weekends. What you'll be doing...

The Abilities Management Case Manager plays an important role in BC Transit’s People and Culture team by supporting employees and leaders through occupational and non-occupational injury and illness claims. In this role, you will provide thoughtful, timely and confidential case management support that helps employees safely remain at work or return to sustainable work as soon as medically appropriate.

You will work closely with employees, leaders, People and Culture partners, Payroll, union representatives, health care providers, WorkSafeBC and insurers to remove barriers, support clear communication and promote early, safe and sustainable return-to-work outcomes.

Your work will include a mix of WorkSafeBC claims, sick leave and short-term illness or injury cases, long-term disability coordination, return-to-work planning and medical accommodation support across unionized and exempt employee groups.

This is a hands-on case management role that requires strong judgment, careful documentation and the ability to manage a high-volume, varied caseload while knowing when to seek guidance or escalate complex matters.

In this position, you will get the opportunity to:
Adjudicate and manage a high volume case load of disability case management activities for occupational and non-occupational injuries and illnesses, with a focus on safe, timely and sustainable return to work.
Maintain regular, supportive communication with employees while collaborating with care providers, leaders and union representatives to understand progress, needs and barriers.
Assess fitness for work using bona fide medical and functional information, to identify opportunities for early intervention, modified duties or accommodation support.
Interpret medical and functional information within the scope of the role and translate restrictions, limitations and abilities into clear, practical workplace recommendations for leaders and employees.
Develop individualized return-to-work plans that reflect an employee’s functional abilities, medical restrictions and individual circumstances.
Document case activity, decisions and next steps in the electronic case management system in a timely, accurate and confidential manner.
Provide expert recommendations, coaching and education on disability management best practices, roles and responsibilities, collective agreement provisions, short-term illness and injury plans, long-term disability and accommodation processes.
Partner with People and Culture Advisors and leaders on medical accommodations by confirming medical restrictions and limitations that support accommodation planning.
Support respectful, solutions-focused conversations when employee needs, medical information, union perspectives and operational requirements need to be aligned.
Collaborate with internal and external partners to resolve complex return-to-work, retraining, alternate employment and accommodation matters.
Balance direct case work with documentation, follow-up, system updates and reporting so that case activity and decisions are clear, accurate and defensible.

This is a hybrid work opportunity with the expectation that the successful candidate will reside in the Greater Victoria and work on-site at least two days per week. There may also be times when attending onsite meetings or connecting with operational teams in person is required to support effective case management and return-to-work planning.

What you might love about this role...

You enjoy working through complex situations and finding practical, people-focused solutions that support employees while also meeting operational needs.
You like variety in your work and are energized by cases that require curiosity, critical thinking, sound judgment and comfort navigating ambiguity.
You find purpose in helping employees stay connected to work or return to work safely, while contributing to attendance, productivity and workforce sustainability.
You are motivated by collaborative work and enjoy partnering with employees, leaders, unions, health care providers and other stakeholders to support meaningful outcomes.
You enjoy converting complex, technical information into clear, practical language that leaders can understand and implement in the workplace.
You appreciate a role where success is built through thoughtful recommendations, strong follow-through, sound judgment and the ability to influence positive outcomes without always being the final decision-maker.

What may not be the right fit...

This work can involve balancing employee needs, operational realities, legal obligations and competing priorities, often while plans continue to evolve.
Many situations are nuanced and require patience, adaptability and the ability to work through uncertainty with care and professionalism.
You can expect to have sensitive conversations, support conflict resolution and help align different perspectives in a respectful and solutions-focused way.
The role requires strong organization and attention to detail, as you will manage multiple complex cases, deadlines and documentation requirements at the same time.

The work includes regular documentation, follow-up and coordination, so candidates should be comfortable balancing people-focused conversations with administrative accuracy and confidentiality.

This role may not be for you if...

You’re looking for a fully remote position or a role with limited need for onsite collaboration, in-person conversations or operational connection.
You’re looking for highly predictable work with limited complexity, few competing priorities and minimal need for problem-solving or decision-making.
You are uncomfortable balancing compassion and employee support with operational requirements, organizational responsibilities and legal obligations.
You find it difficult to manage multiple priorities, adapt to changing circumstances or maintain resilience when plans shift or challenges arise.

What you'll bring to the table...

We value lifelong learners and have found that a mix of any of the following credentials have set people up for success in this role in the past:
To be successful, you’ll bring both technical disability management knowledge and the ability to communicate complex information in a clear, practical and respectful way.

A bachelor’s degree in Disability Management, Human Resources, Kinesiology, Health sciences or a related field, plus two years of recent related experience in disability case management; or a related post-secondary diploma/certificate plus four years of recent related experience.
Experience applying disability management best practices, early intervention principles and return-to-work planning in a unionized environment.
Knowledge of WorkSafeBC claims processing, policies, procedures and the Rehabilitation Services & Claims Manual is considered an asset.
Strong understanding of employment legislation, collective agreements, human rights obligations, privacy requirements and the roles of key stakeholders in the disability management process.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, written communication and verbal communication skills, with excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
Strong ability to interpret complex medical information and translate it into clear, practical workplace recommendations that support accommodation, return to work planning, ensuring leaders can confidently implement solutions that balance employee recovery, operational requirements and legal obligations.

What we'll bring to the table...

Membership in BC’s Public Service Pension Plan (PSPP). Nationally recognized for its strong investment and governance practices, PSPP is a “defined benefit” plan
Access to fitness and lifestyle centers to help you take care of your physical fitness and health
Various programs that support employees such as an Employee Assistance Program and health and wellness initiatives and events aimed at fostering your mental health
A complimentary employee bus pass (plus taxable dependent passes)
A corporate learning and development program to help you in continuous career growth
An employee recognition program where we all recognize each other's successes (not just your Leaders!)
A social club that gives you access to events throughout Victoria

Are we right for you...

Keep reading to find out if this role is meant for you!

What you'll be doing...

The Abilities Management Case Manager plays an important role in BC Transit’s People and Culture team by supporting employees and leaders through occupational and non-occupational injury and illness claims. In this role, you will provide thoughtful, timely and confidential case management support that helps employees safely remain at work or return to sustainable work as soon as medically appropriate.

You will work closely with employees, leaders, People and Culture partners, Payroll, union representatives, health care providers, WorkSafeBC and insurers to remove barriers, support clear communication and promote early, safe and sustainable return-to-work outcomes.

Your work will include a mix of WorkSafeBC claims, sick leave and short-term illness or injury cases, long-term disability coordination, return-to-work planning and medical accommodation support across unionized and exempt employee groups.

This is a hands-on case management role that requires strong judgment, careful documentation and the ability to manage a high-volume, varied caseload while knowing when to seek guidance or escalate complex matters.

In this position, you will get the opportunity to:
Adjudicate and manage a high volume case load of disability case management activities for occupational and non-occupational injuries and illnesses, with a focus on safe, timely and sustainable return to work.
Maintain regular, supportive communication with employees while collaborating with care providers, leaders and union representatives to understand progress, needs and barriers.
Assess fitness for work using bona fide medical and functional information, to identify opportunities for early intervention, modified duties or accommodation support.
Interpret medical and functional information within the scope of the role and translate restrictions, limitations and abilities into clear, practical workplace recommendations for leaders and employees.
Develop individualized return-to-work plans that reflect an employee’s functional abilities, medical restrictions and individual circumstances.
Document case activity, decisions and next steps in the electronic case management system in a timely, accurate and confidential manner.
Provide expert recommendations, coaching and education on disability management best practices, roles and responsibilities, collective agreement provisions, short-term illness and injury plans, long-term disability and accommodation processes.
Partner with People and Culture Advisors and leaders on medical accommodations by confirming medical restrictions and limitations that support accommodation planning.
Support respectful, solutions-focused conversations when employee needs, medical information, union perspectives and operational requirements need to be aligned.
Collaborate with internal and external partners to resolve complex return-to-work, retraining, alternate employment and accommodation matters.
Balance direct case work with documentation, follow-up, system updates and reporting so that case activity and decisions are clear, accurate and defensible.

This is a hybrid work opportunity with the expectation that the successful candidate will reside in the Greater Victoria and work on-site at least two days per week. There may also be times when attending onsite meetings or connecting with operational teams in person is required to support effective case management and return-to-work planning.

What you might love about this role...

You enjoy working through complex situations and finding practical, people-focused solutions that support employees while also meeting operational needs.
You like variety in your work and are energized by cases that require curiosity, critical thinking, sound judgment and comfort navigating ambiguity.
You find purpose in helping employees stay connected to work or return to work safely, while contributing to attendance, productivity and workforce sustainability.
You are motivated by collaborative work and enjoy partnering with employees, leaders, unions, health care providers and other stakeholders to support meaningful outcomes.
You enjoy converting complex, technical information into clear, practical language that leaders can understand and implement in the workplace.
You appreciate a role where success is built through thoughtful recommendations, strong follow-through, sound judgment and the ability to influence positive outcomes without always being the final decision-maker.

What may not be the right fit...

This work can involve balancing employee needs, operational realities, legal obligations and competing priorities, often while plans continue to evolve.
Many situations are nuanced and require patience, adaptability and the ability to work through uncertainty with care and professionalism.
You can expect to have sensitive conversations, support conflict resolution and help align different perspectives in a respectful and solutions-focused way.
The role requires strong organization and attention to detail, as you will manage multiple complex cases, deadlines and documentation requirements at the same time.

The work includes regular documentation, follow-up and coordination, so candidates should be comfortable balancing people-focused conversations with administrative accuracy and confidentiality.

This role may not be for you if...

You’re looking for a fully remote position or a role with limited need for onsite collaboration, in-person conversations or operational connection.
You’re looking for highly predictable work with limited complexity, few competing priorities and minimal need for problem-solving or decision-making.
You are uncomfortable balancing compassion and employee support with operational requirements, organizational responsibilities and legal obligations.
You find it difficult to manage multiple priorities, adapt to changing circumstances or maintain resilience when plans shift or challenges arise.

What you'll bring to the table...

We value lifelong learners and have found that a mix of any of the following credentials have set people up for success in this role in the past:
To be successful, you’ll bring both technical disability management knowledge and the ability to communicate complex information in a clear, practical and respectful way.

A bachelor’s degree in Disability Management, Human Resources, Kinesiology, Health sciences or a related field, plus two years of recent related experience in disability case management; or a related post-secondary diploma/certificate plus four years of recent related experience.
Experience applying disability management best practices, early intervention principles and return-to-work planning in a unionized environment.
Knowledge of WorkSafeBC claims processing, policies, procedures and the Rehabilitation Services & Claims Manual is considered an asset.
Strong understanding of employment legislation, collective agreements, human rights obligations, privacy requirements and the roles of key stakeholders in the disability management process.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, written communication and verbal communication skills, with excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
Strong ability to interpret complex medical information and translate it into clear, practical workplace recommendations that support accommodation, return to work planning, ensuring leaders can confidently implement solutions that balance employee recovery, operational requirements and legal obligations.

What we'll bring to the table...

A complimentary employee bus pass (plus taxable dependent passes)

A social club that gives you access to events throughout Victoria

The Children and Families Department takes a strengths-based approach to working with each other, children, young people and families, and our partner agencies. We call this 'Our Nottinghamshire Approach'. Watch the two minute animation to learn more.

Nottinghamshire County Council
is dedicated to making a positive impact in our communities. We pride ourselves on being rooted in community, providing essential services that improve lives every day. Join us in our mission to support children, young people, and families in need.

We are seeking a passionate Social Worker
to join our Assessment Team in the Broxtowe & Rushcliffe Family Support and Safeguarding Team. In this mid-level role, you will work closely with children, young people, and their families/carers. Your primary responsibility will be to plan and lead assessments that identify strengths, resilience, vulnerabilities, developmental needs, and risks. This is an exciting opportunity to make a real difference in the lives of those you serve.

As a Social Worker, Your Key Responsibilities Will Include

Conducting Comprehensive Assessments: Gather and analyse information to evaluate the strengths and vulnerabilities of children and families.
Coordinating Support Services: Work collaboratively with families and partners to identify and implement strategies and interventions that meet their needs.
Writing Reports: Prepare structured, evidence-based reports, including Child and Family Assessments and documentation for Initial Child Protection Conferences.
Managing Workload: Organise and manage your caseload independently while receiving supervision from the Team Manager.

To Be Successful In This Role, You Will Need

A Professional Social Work Qualification (e.g., DipSW, CQSW, CSS).
Registration with Social Work England.
Experience in child protection, safeguarding, and assessment work.
A full driving licence and access to a vehicle for work purposes.

We Are Looking For Candidates Who Demonstrate

Strong Communication Skills: Ability to engage effectively with children, families, and colleagues.
Analytical Thinking: Capability to make informed decisions based on evidence and assessments.
Empathy and Compassion: A genuine desire to support and uplift vulnerable individuals and families.
Team Collaboration: Willingness to work as part of a multi-disciplinary team to achieve the best outcomes.

At Nottinghamshire County Council, We Offer

A Place to Belong: A friendly, inclusive workplace where everyone is valued.
Professional Development: Opportunities for ongoing training and career advancement.
Flexible Working: A supportive environment that promotes work-life balance.
Generous Leave: Competitive annual leave and benefits to support your well-being.

Help Change a Child’s Story
Are you passionate about supporting children and families within the foster care system? Join our team as a Foster Care Case Manager
and make a lasting difference in the lives of youth by providing stability, advocacy, and compassionate support.
In this role, you’ll manage your own caseload, work closely with families and community partners, and play a critical role in helping children find safe and supportive environments.
Why This Role Matters
Every child deserves safety, stability, and the opportunity to thrive. As a Foster Care Case Manager, you’ll be a trusted advocate—helping guide children and families through challenging transitions while ensuring their voices are heard and their needs are met.
What You’ll Do
Case Management & Client Support

Manage a caseload of foster care cases, providing ongoing support and advocacy
Build relationships with children, caregivers, and families to support stability and well-being
Offer guidance, referrals, and mentoring to those involved in each case

Placement Coordination & Court Involvement

Coordinate initial placements and any necessary changes in placement
Prepare for and attend court hearings, providing updates and documentation
Support children and caregivers through transitions with hands-on involvement

Collaboration & Communication

Partner with referral sources, courts, agencies, and community organizations
Maintain consistent communication with all stakeholders involved in each case
Advocate for appropriate services and support systems

Documentation & Compliance

Maintain accurate and timely case records, reports, and required documentation
Track client progress and ensure compliance with all program and regulatory standards

What You Bring
Bachelor’s degree in Social Work or related human services field required

State of Michigan licensure preferred

At least 1 year of experience in child welfare preferred

Strong interpersonal, organizational, and documentation skills
Ability to work independently while managing a dynamic caseload

Additional Requirements
Valid, unrestricted driver’s license with a good driving record
Reliable personal transportation and current automobile insurance
Willingness to participate in a 24-hour on-call support system as needed

What Sets You Apart
Passion for working with children and families
Ability to navigate complex, emotionally challenging situations
Strong advocacy and problem-solving skills
Commitment to making a difference in the lives of youth

Make a Difference That Lasts
If you're ready to take on meaningful, impactful work and help shape brighter futures for children in foster care, we’d love to meet you.
Apply today and help change a child’s story!
